conversation_history.content: Mera naamVikram Singh hai. Maine 10 September ko VoltRide Motors Pvt Ltd se Rs. 1,45,000 ka electric scooter kharida tha (Invoice #VR-9981). 15 din me hi uski battery dead ho gayi aur scooter chalna band ho gaya. Service center ne warranty me replace karne se mana kar diya aur bol rahe hain naya battery pack ke Rs. 60,000 lagenge. Mere paas GST tax invoice, warranty card aur service center job sheet hai.

विक्रम, आपने जो facts बताए हैं, उसके हिसाब से आपकी position बहुत strong है। 10 September को आपने Rs. 1,45,000 में जो scooter लिया था, उसकी battery सिर्फ 15 दिन के अंदर dead हो जाना सीधा-सीधा manufacturing defect (Section 2(10) CPA 2019) और deficiency in service (Section 2(11) CPA 2019) का मामला है। Service center का यह कहना कि आपको new battery pack के लिए Rs. 60,000 देने होंगे, पूरी तरह से एक Unfair Trade Practice (Section 2(47) CPA 2019) है। आपका primary claim Rs. 1,45,000 का full refund या free replacement का है, और यह Rs. 60,000 का amount आपके original claim के against set-off नहीं हो सकता। 

आपके पास जो GST tax invoice (#VR-9981), warranty card और service center job sheet है, ये primary documentary evidence हैं। अगर ये documents PDF या email format में हैं, तो court में formally admit कराने के लिए हमें Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 के Section 63 के तहत एक certificate attach करना होगा। 

आगे legal notice draft करने और e-Daakhil portal पर complaint file करने के लिए, मुझे बस यह जानना है कि आप currently किस city में रहते हैं और VoltRide Motors का कौन सा branch या head office आपके area के करीब है?

facts.product_or_service_details: Electric scooter purchased on 10 September (Invoice #VR-9981); battery failed within 15 days and scooter became non-operational
facts.nature_of_grievance: Defective product (battery dead within 15 days), refusal to honor warranty replacement, and demand for Rs. 60,000 for a new battery pack instead of a free replacement
facts._calculation_note: No pro-rata or multi-component arithmetic is required at this stage. The client has stated a single upfront purchase price of Rs. 1,45,000. Under Section 2(10) and 2(11) of the CPA 2019, a unilateral refusal to replace a defective battery within the warranty period constitutes a 'defect' and 'deficiency in service', entitling the consumer to a full refund or free replacement. The Rs. 60,000 quoted by the service center for a new battery pack is irrelevant to the consumer's primary claim for the defective unit and cannot be set off against the original purchase price.
facts._doctrinal_analysis: Substantive Doctrine: The sale of a defective electric scooter within 15 days attracts strict liability under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (Sections 2(10), 2(11), and 20), rendering the unilateral 'No Return/No Refund' or warranty-denial stance of VoltRide Motors void and unconscionable. Forum & Jurisdiction: The consumer may file via e-Daakhil in the District Commission having territorial jurisdiction where he resides or works for gain (Section 34(2)(d) CPA 2019), avoiding travel to the seller's head office. Limitation: The cause of action arose on or around 10 September; the 2-year limitation period under Section 69 CPA 2019 remains available. Evidentiary Strategy: The GST tax invoice, warranty card, and service center job sheet constitute primary documentary evidence; a Section 63 Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 certificate will be required to formally admit these electronic/digital records if they are in PDF/email format.
facts._case_nuances: The defect manifested extremely rapidly (within 15 days of purchase), establishing a clear manufacturing/latent defect. The service center explicitly refused warranty replacement and instead demanded payment of Rs. 60,000 for a new battery pack. The consumer possesses the original GST tax invoice (VR-9981), the physical warranty card, and the service center job sheet, providing a robust evidentiary basis for a refund or replacement claim.

state_snapshot.legal_notice_draft:
**WITHOUT PREJUDICE**

**FORMAL LEGAL NOTICE OF DEMAND**
*(Dispatched via Registered Post A.D. / Speed Post / Registered Email / WhatsApp under Section 27 of the General Clauses Act, 1897)*

**Date:** 08 November, 2026

**To:**
VoltRide Motors Pvt Ltd,
Hazratganj Showroom, Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh

**From (Claimant / Noticee Sender):**
Vikram Singh,
Resident of Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh

**SUBJECT:** DEMAND FOR REFUND OF RS. 1,45,000/- AND FREE WARRANTY REPLACEMENT OF DEFECTIVE ELECTRIC SCOOTER (INVOICE #VR-9981) IN VIOLATION OF CONSUMER PROTECTION ACT, 2019, SECTION 74 INDIAN CONTRACT ACT, 1872, AND NOTICE OF INTENTION TO INSTITUTE PROCEEDINGS BEFORE THE DISTRICT CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION, LUCKNOW

1. **FACTS OF THE CASE AND CAUSE OF ACTION:**
   The undersigned, Vikram Singh, is a bona fide consumer residing in Lucknow. On 10 September, the undersigned purchased an electric scooter from the Opposite Party, VoltRide Motors Pvt Ltd (Hazratganj, Lucknow), bearing Invoice Number VR-9981, for a single upfront purchase price of Rs. 1,45,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Forty-Five Thousand Only). The said purchase was supported by a formal Tax Invoice and a corresponding payment receipt. 

2. **DEFECT AND DEFICIENCY IN SERVICE:**
   Within a mere 15 days of the aforementioned transaction, specifically around 25 September, the battery of the said electric scooter failed completely, rendering the vehicle entirely non-operational. The rapid manifestation of this defect within 15 days of purchase establishes a clear manufacturing and/or latent defect in the product. 

3. **REFUSAL TO HONOR WARRANTY AND UNFAIR TRADE PRACTICE:**
   Upon reporting the defect to the Opposite Party’s service center, the service center explicitly refused to honor the warranty replacement. Instead of providing a free replacement under the warranty terms, the service center arbitrarily demanded a sum of Rs. 60,000/- (Rupees Sixty Thousand Only) from the undersigned for a new battery pack. 

4. **FINANCIAL CLAIM AND DOCTRINAL BASIS:**
   The undersigned’s primary claim is for a full refund of the original purchase price of Rs. 1,45,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Forty-Five Thousand Only), or alternatively, a free replacement of the defective unit. Under Section 2(10) and 2(11) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, the dead battery within 15 days constitutes a 'defect' and a 'deficiency in service'. The unilateral refusal to replace the defective battery within the warranty period entitles the consumer to a full refund or free replacement. The Rs. 60,000/- quoted by the service center for a new battery pack is entirely irrelevant to the consumer's primary claim for the defective unit and cannot be set off against the original purchase price of Rs. 1,45,000/-. Furthermore, under Section 2(47) of the CPA 2019, demanding Rs. 60,000/- for a warranty-covered defect constitutes an Unfair Trade Practice. As per the principles laid down in *Pioneer Urban Land & Infrastructure Ltd. vs. Govindan Raghavan (2019) 5 SCC 725*, one-sided, unfair clauses in standard-form consumer contracts, such as arbitrary refusal to honor warranties, constitute an Unfair Trade Practice under the Consumer Protection Act. Additionally, the arbitrary demand of Rs. 60,000/- is an unconscionable penalty attempt under Section 74 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, which is legally unenforceable without proof of actual loss.

5. **EVIDENTIARY BASIS:**
   The undersigned relies upon the original GST Tax Invoice (VR-9981), the physical warranty card, and the service center job sheet as primary documentary evidence. All digital and electronic records, including UPI/NEFT bank statements, e-commerce order confirmations, and any correspondence (WhatsApp, emails), have been meticulously preserved and are admissible upon certification under **Section 63 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023**.

6. **JURISDICTION AND LIMITATION:**
   Pursuant to Section 34(2)(d) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, territorial jurisdiction for this dispute lies before the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission at Lucknow, as the undersigned resides in Lucknow. The Opposite Party’s Hazratganj showroom is also located within this jurisdiction. The cause of action arose on 25 September, and this notice is being dispatched well within the statutory limitation period of two years prescribed under Section 69 of the CPA 2019. Should the Opposite Party fail to comply, the complaint shall be filed via the e-Daakhil portal in the Lucknow District Commission.

7. **DEMAND AND STATUTORY CURE CLAUSE:**
   In light of the aforementioned facts, defects, and deficiencies in service, the Opposite Party is hereby called upon to:
   a) Refund the entire purchase price of **Rs. 1,45,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Forty-Five Thousand Only)** within **15 (fifteen) days** from the receipt of this notice; and/or
   b) Provide a free, unconditional replacement of the defective electric scooter/battery unit within the aforementioned 15-day period.
   
   Failing such compliance, the undersigned shall be constrained to initiate appropriate civil and/or consumer proceedings before the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Lucknow. In the event of such litigation, the Opposite Party shall be liable to pay the principal amount of **Rs. 1,45,000/-** along with interest at the rate of **18% per annum** from the date of cause of action, in accordance with Section 34 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. All costs, damages, and consequences of such proceedings shall be borne by the Opposite Party at its sole risk.

**Dated this 08th day of November, 2026.**

Vikram Singh
Claimant / Noticee Sender
